Best For: Most web apps needing structured data with relationships, transactions, and strong consistency — SaaS, e-commerce, dashboards, any app with users/orders/products.
Tradeoffs: Huge ecosystem, mature, well-supported, excellent for complex queries.

Best For: Read-heavy web apps, widely used in existing stacks, simple CRUD apps.
Tradeoffs: Less advanced features than PostgreSQL; weaker for complex queries and advanced transactions.
Default For: Alternative to PostgreSQL; widely used but PostgreSQL is generally recommended for new apps.

Best For: Local development, small apps, mobile/desktop apps, embedded use cases, offline-first apps.
Tradeoffs: Single file, no server needed, easy to set up, zero infrastructure.
Default For: Default for local dev, small apps, mobile/desktop, offline-first.

Best For: Document-heavy apps, flexible/evolving schema, content-heavy apps, rapid prototyping where schema changes frequently.
Tradeoffs: Flexible schema, good for unstructured data, horizontal scaling.
Default For: Alternative when data is document-heavy and schema flexibility matters more than consistency.

Best For: Quick-start apps, apps needing auth + database + storage + realtime in one, small teams wanting minimal backend code.
Tradeoffs: PostgreSQL under the hood with built-in auth, storage, realtime, good DX, generous free tier.
Default For: Alternative for simple apps wanting auth + database + storage without building a backend.

Best For: Mobile-first apps, real-time sync needs, quick-start apps, simple apps.
Tradeoffs: Real-time sync, good mobile SDKs, easy to start, Google-backed.
ORM Pairs: Firebase SDK (no ORM — direct SDK usage).
Default For: Alternative for mobile-first or real-time-heavy apps.

Best For: Caching, session storage, rate limiting, ephemeral data, pub/sub, job queues.
Default For: Not a primary database — use alongside PostgreSQL/MySQL for caching, sessions, rate limiting.

Best For: Apps needing serverless PostgreSQL with branching, good DX, separate backend apps that benefit from pay-per-use pricing.
Tradeoffs: Serverless PostgreSQL, branching (like Git for data), scales to zero, Postgres-compatible.
Default For: Alternative for separate-backend apps wanting serverless PostgreSQL.
